title: Tentative swap fuse with rate-limited shadow drain and snapshot rollback
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: rolling canary handoffs currently observe a small but measurable window where sessions routed to a canary experience partial KV-cache misses and out-of-order prefix replay. This PR introduces a 'tentative swap fuse' that coordinates a deterministic handoff sequence: (1) a rate-limited shadow drain window to warm caches and detect regressions, (2) a tentative (non-committal) swap that labels traffic as active-but-revocable, and (3) a snapshot rollback snapshot + playbook that can be triggered automatically if safety gates fail. The intent is to reduce flakiness during canary -> primary swaps, enable deterministic A/B toggles tied to session affinity, and provide a fast automated rollback path that relies on captured checkpoint snapshots.
commits: a3b9f7d: introduce tentative swap state machine and API hooks
e7c2b1f: implement rate-limited shadow drain proxy and metrics
c5d4a0b: add snapshot capture and restore utilities (rollback helpers)
f2a1d3e: tests: integration flow for shadow->tentative->commit/rollback
review_comments: Diego Morales (reviewer): Nice decomposition. Two asks: (1) can we expose the tentative-swap TTL as a per-release config and not hardcode 30s? (2) please add a high-cardinality tag to the 'shadow_drain_success' metric to avoid aggregation confusion.

Maya Patel (author): Added values.yaml entry and made TTL configurable via chart + CRD (defaults to 30s). Also added 'release_id' tag to the metric; refactored metrics export to include release_id and cohort_id.

Anika Shah (reviewer): Integration test is flakey in CI occasionally; observed a deadlock when the snapshot restore fails mid-handshake. Can we make the snapshot restore asynchronous and limit concurrent restores?
Maya Patel (author): Converted restore to a background worker with an in-flight limiter (default 2). Added retry/backoff and stronger assertions in the integration test to avoid timing races.

Ravi Kothari (reviewer): Safety gates look solid but we need an 'operator override' flag documented precisely so SREs know how to force a commit in emergencies. Also, add a circuit-breaker metric when tentative swaps are aborted by rollback.

Maya Patel (author): Added operator_override boolean to CRD and documented fail-open vs fail-closed behaviors in the operator runbook. Added 'tentative_swap_aborts_total' metric and alert suggestion in docs.
Integration CI (comment): integration-tests failed on first run due to flakey ordering in seq_handshake_test.go. Rerun triggered.
CI Bot (comment): integration-tests passed on rerun. All checks green.
merge_outcome: Merged by squash with commit message: 'tentative swap fuse + rate-limited shadow drain and snapshot rollback; ENG-2148; closes SUP-4021'
release_notes: Introduce tentative-swap handshake to reduce transient cache misses during canary handoffs; add rate-limited shadow drain to warm caches; add snapshot-based rollback utilities and an operator runbook. Backwards-compatible; rollout opt-in via CRD and chart values.
notes_for_ops: Operator runbook added at docs/runbooks/rollback-playbook.md. Default behavior is opt-in via chart flag 'rollout.tentativeSwap.enabled=false'. Operators can enable per-environment, tune TTL and concurrency via the CRD fields 'tentativeSwap.ttlSeconds' and 'tentativeSwap.concurrentRestores'. In case of automatic rollback, snapshotter will emit 'rollout.rollback.snapshot_id' tag for forensic playback.
qa_summary:
- Unit tests added for state machine transitions.
- Integration test simulates shadow drain and tentative commit followed by forced restore path.
- Manual QA: deployed on canary cluster, exercised A/B fallback by toggling operator_override; verified metrics and rollback-triggered snapshot restores.
manual_migration_steps: None required. New CRD fields are additive. To opt-in: update chart values and set rollout.tentativeSwap.enabled=true and apply CRD. Existing rollouts unaffected.
changelog_entry: Feature: tentative swap fuse with shadow drain and snapshot rollback (opt-in) — adds safer deterministic canary handoffs and fast automated rollback
extra_context: This PR is part of a small initiative (ENG-2148) to reduce canary-induced customer-facing errors by making handoffs deterministic and observable. Follow-up work: (a) extend tentative swap to multi-region handoffs, (b) add replay harness for snapshot forensic validation.
